title: Write anchor text that describes the destination
statement: The visible text of an internal link states what the linked page is, so the link remains meaningful when read on its own, and generic wording such as click here or read more is replaced or supplemented with an accessible name.
rationale: The anchor text is the only description of a destination available before it is fetched, and a link whose text carries no information forces both readers and crawlers to fetch the page to learn whether it was worth following.
implementation: Replace the generic phrase with the destination title, or keep the phrase and attach the accessible name through an attribute so assistive technology reports the destination. For icon-only links, supply the name rather than relying on the icon.

verification.method: Collect the accessible name of every internal link in the served response and report links whose name is empty or matches a known generic phrase.

sources.title: Make your links crawlable, place descriptive text inside the anchor

title: Keep internal links pointing at URLs that resolve
statement: Every internal link target returns a successful response or a deliberate single redirect, and no internal link points at a path that returns a client or server error.
rationale: A broken internal link is a path the site itself offers and then fails to honour, which wastes the fetch and leaves the destination unreachable through the route the site advertised.
implementation: Resolve link targets through the route definitions at build time where the framework allows it, so a removed route breaks the build rather than the site. For content-authored links, crawl the internal graph on a schedule and correct or remove the failing targets.

verification.method: Request every internal link target found while crawling the site and record the status code and redirect chain for each one.

sources.title: HTTP status codes, network and DNS errors

title: Expose a breadcrumb trail on deeply nested pages
statement: A page more than one level below the site root shows its ancestor path as real links, and any breadcrumb markup describes the same trail the page displays.
rationale: The trail is what lets a reader arriving directly on a deep page move up into the section it belongs to, and it gives that page an inbound link from every descendant rather than only from a listing.
implementation: Derive the trail from the route hierarchy rather than from a hand-written list per page, and emit the markup from the same derived structure so the two cannot disagree. Do not invent an intermediate level that has no page behind it.

verification.method: Compare the visible breadcrumb links in the response against the marked-up trail and against the route hierarchy for the same page.

caution: The cited documentation specifies how to mark up a breadcrumb trail that exists. It does not state that a site must have one, so the requirement to show a trail on deep pages is tier B rather than tier A.

title: Avoid linking prominently to routes excluded from the index
statement: Navigation, listings, and body content do not present routes that carry an index-suppressing directive as ordinary destinations, and links that must remain for readers are confined to the context where they are needed.
rationale: A site-wide link to a page it has asked to keep out of the index sends every crawl toward a destination that will be discarded, and the contradiction is easy to introduce because both halves look correct in isolation.
implementation: Cross-reference the navigation link set against the set of routes marked for exclusion, and move any overlap out of shared layout components. Do not resolve the overlap by removing the exclusion directive unless the page is genuinely meant to be indexed.

verification.method: Fetch every route linked from shared navigation and report those whose response or markup carries an index-suppressing directive.

caution: The cited documentation describes how exclusion directives work but does not prohibit linking to an excluded page. The recommendation to keep such links out of shared navigation reflects crawl efficiency rather than a published rule.

title: Keep every indexable page within a bounded click depth
statement: Each indexable page is reachable from the site root by following a small declared number of links, and the site records what that bound is rather than leaving depth to emerge from the navigation it happens to have.
rationale: Depth is a property of the link graph that nobody chooses deliberately, so pages drift further from the root as sections grow, and the pages hardest to reach are the ones a crawl is least likely to revisit.
implementation: Compute depth from the crawled internal graph, pick a bound the site can hold, and add hub or index pages where a section exceeds it. Adding links purely to shorten a path, without a reader who would follow them, does not count as a fix.

verification.method: Traverse the internal link graph breadth-first from the root and report the depth distribution together with any indexable page beyond the declared bound.

caution: No documented crawl depth limit exists. The cited page states that well-linked and popular URLs tend to be crawled more often, which supports reducing depth as a direction without establishing any specific bound, so confidence here is low by design.

sources.title: Large site owner's guide to managing your crawl budget
